the diffusion/perfusion volume mismatch is a useful indicator in experimental focal cerebral infarction, and the mismatch can be used to predict infarct volumes in experimental stroke models.

the diffusion/perfusion mismatches are transient in both permanent and temporary focal ischemia models.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the diffusion/perfusion ratio is not a reliable indicator of tissue at risk of infarction in the permanent MCA occlusion model, but it is a reliable indicator of the tissue at risk of ischemic injury in the 60‐minute transient MCA occlusion group.
the diffusion/perfusion ratio in focal cerebral ischemia models depends on both the duration and type of occlusion.
DWI and PWI are useful tools in evaluating the diffusion/perfusion mismatches in the early stage of experimental ischemic stroke.
